niche: a gemeente's prognosis to the province of its first year of social rental production counted on WWS points, measured as the growth of the social rental stock between 1 January and 31 December against the regional housing agreement's tranche
answer: expected inhaalopgave of 112 sociale huurwoningen carried into 2028 (taakstelling 2027 of 190; growth 78 = 261 put into use less 183 that leave once: 38 demolished, 131 in the 2027 heat-plan blocks lifted over 143 or sold first, 14 verkoopvijver sales outside the blocks; 15 verkoopvijver dwellings sold in 2027 stand in blocks B2 and B7)
stakeholder_role: the gemeente's senior policy adviser for housing, who files the woondeal monitor and the province's prognosis

driver: Two dated schedules held in separate files under different keys each remove members from one population, a disposal list and an upgrade programme, and a subset of members stands in both, disposed of before the upgrade reaches them; summing the two lists removes that subset twice, and only a member-level join between a code-keyed list and an address-keyed list exposes it, while every closed period's additive flow sum was exact because the upgrade channel did not exist then.
driver_concrete: Peelvenne's 2027 social rental production is the growth of the number of rental dwellings with at most 143 WWS points; Velmaro sells the dwellings of its verkoopvijver, let on temporary Leegstandwet contracts, as each permit ends, and some of them stand in two blocks of the heat-transition plan that complete after the sale; the closed monitors' flow model was exact because on rent no renovation moved a dwelling, but in 2027 the renovation and the sales both take dwellings out of the social stock and the sold dwellings inside the blocks leave once though they appear in both lists; a complex Velmaro sells to an investor with its tenants stays social whoever lets it.
stump: A competent solver lifts the renovated dwellings over 143 out of the social stock, takes the verkoopvijver's 2027 sales from the Leegstandwet permits that end in 2027, and subtracts both, never checking whether the dwellings sold in 2027 stand in the blocks the packages renovate; some do, and they complete after the sale, so it subtracts those dwellings twice and files an inhaalopgave too high by their number, and higher again if it withdraws the complex sold to an investor with its tenants.

differentiation.task102: task102 moves scheduled payments across a period end by a release rule only the payment history shows; v7 moves no timing across the period end, it removes double-listed units from a within-period flow sum
differentiation.task98: v6 turned on a population absent from every flow list (renovated dwellings lifted over 143, read off twins); v7 keeps that as depth and turns on a population present in two flow lists at once (verkoopvijver dwellings sold before their heat-plan block completes), named by complex code in one file and by address range in the other, so only a dwelling-level join finds it

lineage.driver: A persons-denominated target for a period is partly met by arrivals who register with members already in place and so count without consuming a unit, and by arrivals who join listed units once those are served, so the units the period needs are a prefix of the ordered list that the natural one-unit-per-listed-household count overstates, and no closed period can show it because the arrival channel had not yet opened.
